data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Bhargava’, which refers to the sage Bhargava or the God Bharga. Bhargava is a title given to sages, seers, and poets, who were believed to have mastered the Vedas. This name signifies dedication and devotion to the wisdom of the Vedas and the gods. The name Bhargvika carries the meaning “Dedicated to Bhargava” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhargvika usually hope their child will grow to embody dedicated to bhargava and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: The Mahabharata, a Sanskrit epic poem composed between 400 BCE and 200 CE, mentions the name Bhargvika as one of the wives of Bhishma Pitamaha. Bhishma was a grand old warrior, the grandsire of the Kuru dynasty, and a central figure in the great battle of Kurukshetra.

The Natyashastra, an ancient Indian treatise on theatre arts written by Bharata Muni around 200 CE, includes Bhargvika as a name of a Rasa (emotion) or a type of dance. In this context, she represents the Rasa of Sringara (love) and is often depicted as an Apsara (heavenly nymph) or a courtesan.
